questions.q: In a built-up area, the name of a district is written on a white background on a direction sign. What does this mean?
options: This district is in the same city
The route there is along a motorway
You can get there only in daytime
The road there is temporarily closed
questions.explain: On signs in a built-up area, a white background means that the place is in the same built-up area. A green or blue background means that after leaving the city the route will be along a motorway or another road.
questions.ref: Annex 1, Chapter 5 (background colour of direction signs)

questions.q: You have entered a village and passed this sign. May you sound the horn to warn a truck ahead that you are going to overtake?
options: Yes, if the truck is driving slowly
No: you may not sound the horn like this in a built-up area
Yes: a warning about overtaking may be given anywhere
No: any overtaking is banned in a village
questions.explain: Sign 5.22 means that the rules for built-up areas start to apply. The horn to warn of overtaking is allowed only outside built-up areas; here you may flash the headlights.

questions.q: You are driving a passenger car and have entered a village past this sign on a blue background. The road has no central reservation, and there are no other signs. What is the highest speed you may drive at?
options: 60 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 5.24 marks a built-up area in which the requirements of the Rules for built-up areas do not apply on this road, including the 60 km/h limit. For a passenger car, the limit outside built-up areas on a road without a central reservation remains: 100 km/h.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. How can you tell whether you may use the middle lane?
options: By the sign at the end of the section ahead
The middle lane is always only for oncoming traffic
By the direction of the vehicles in the adjacent lane
By the lane-control signal above that lane
questions.explain: Sign 5.35 marks a section where the direction of traffic in one or more lanes may be reversed. Whether you may use such a lane is shown by the lane-control signals above it.

questions.q: This sign informs you about photo and video enforcement of violations. May a camera record a violation where there is no such sign?
options: No: without a sign, enforcement is unlawful
Only if the sign is 150-300 m away
Only in built-up areas
Yes: placing this sign is not mandatory
questions.explain: According to the text for sign 5.42 (as amended by Order No. 305, in force from 12.07.2026), violations are recorded by a stationary certified technical device, and placing the sign itself is not mandatory. So a camera may operate where there is no sign.

questions.q: You have passed sign 5.44 “Parking restriction zone” and then two intersections. Sign 5.45 has not appeared yet. May you park here?
options: Yes: the zone ended at the first intersection
No: the ban lasts until the end-of-zone sign
Yes, if you park for less than 30 minutes
Only on the right side of the street
questions.explain: Sign 5.44 marks the start of an area where parking is banned. Such a ban does not end at an intersection; it applies throughout the zone up to sign 5.45 “End of parking restriction zone”.

questions.q: Who is allowed to travel in a pedestrian zone, the start of which is marked by sign 5.48?
options: Everyone, but no faster than 20 km/h
Pedestrians and taxis
Only pedestrians
Pedestrians and cyclists
questions.explain: Sign 5.48 marks the place where an area begins in which only pedestrians are allowed. Do not confuse it with residential zone 5.38, where vehicles drive at no more than 20 km/h.

questions.q: At the entrance to a zone there is sign 5.50 with an environmental class restriction. The registration documents of your car do not state an environmental class. May you enter?
options: Yes: if no class is stated, the ban does not apply to you
Yes, but only on weekends
Yes, if the car is less than five years old
No: entry is banned for such vehicles too
questions.explain: Sign 5.50 bans motor vehicles whose environmental class is lower than the one shown on the sign, or is not stated in the registration documents.

questions.q: You have passed a sign with a plate, as in the diagram. At the edge of the carriageway before the crossing, a person is signalling with a white cane: they are about to cross. What should you do?
options: Stop and let them cross
Drive on before they step onto the carriageway
Sound the horn so that they wait
Let them cross only if they are already on the “zebra”
questions.explain: Plate 7.15 under sign 1.20 warns that the crossing is used by people who are completely blind. A driver must give way to a completely blind pedestrian who signals with a white cane in all cases, even away from a pedestrian crossing.

questions.q: You need a vehicle service station. How do you get there, judging by the sign with a plate?
options: Drive straight on: the station is 200 m ahead by the road
Turn right: the station is 200 m off to the side
Turn left: the station is 200 m off to the side
Make a U-turn: the station is 200 m behind you
questions.explain: Plate 7.1.3 shows the distance to an object that is to the side of the road, and the arrow shows which way to turn towards it. Here the service station is 200 m to the right.

questions.q: What does this sign require of the driver?
options: Reduce speed to 40 km/h
Stop at the place to eat
Give way to vehicles leaving the parking area
Nothing: it only informs about a place to eat
questions.explain: Service signs only inform you about the location of facilities: a place to eat, a filling station, vehicle service and others. By themselves they neither ban nor require anything.

questions.q: You are driving in the lane next to a lane for route vehicles and have passed this sign. May you now move into the right lane, if there are no other bans?
options: No: the right lane is for buses up to the intersection
Only to turn right
Yes: the lane for route vehicles has ended here
No: only taxis and buses may use it
questions.explain: Sign 5.9.1 marks the end of a lane for route vehicles. Before it, ordinary cars could not use that lane; beyond the sign it is an ordinary lane, and you may move into it.

questions.q: Sign 2.1 “Priority road” hangs above the carriageway. Where is plate 7.13 “Direction of the priority road” placed in this case?
options: Under the sign, as usual
To the side of the sign
On a separate post beyond the intersection
Such a plate is not hung above the road
questions.explain: Plates are placed directly under the sign. Exception: plates 7.2.2-7.2.4 and 7.13, for signs above the carriageway, shoulder or pavement, are placed to the side of the sign.

questions.q: This sign with a plate hangs above the right lane. Whom does the restriction concern?
options: Everyone travelling in this direction
Only those travelling in this lane
Only trucks in the right lane
Only those turning right
questions.explain: Plate 7.14 shows the traffic lane to which the sign or traffic light applies. The 40 km/h limit concerns only the right lane.

questions.q: Besides route vehicles, who may drive past this sign with a plate?
options: A taxi taking a passenger to their home
Passenger cars of residents of this street
Cars with the “Person with a disability” sign
Trucks delivering goods to local shops
questions.explain: Plate 7.18 means that the sign does not apply to motorised wheelchairs and cars with the “Person with a disability” identification sign. For all others, except route vehicles, entry is banned.

questions.q: Before an intersection there is a permanent sign 4.1.1 “Ahead only”, and next to it, on a portable stand, a temporary sign 4.1.2 “Turn right only” on a yellow background. Which way do you go?
options: Only straight ahead: the permanent sign is more important
Straight ahead or right, as you choose
Only right: the temporary sign is obeyed
Stop and wait for instructions
questions.explain: If the meanings of temporary signs on a portable stand and of fixed signs contradict each other, drivers follow the temporary ones. This is how a work site is usually bypassed.

questions.q: You are driving on a roundabout with this sign and have passed the exit you need. What should you do?
options: Drive another lap and leave where you need to
Reverse to the missed exit
Make a U-turn and go back to the exit against the arrows
Stop and wait until the exit is free
questions.explain: Sign 4.3 allows movement only in the direction of the arrows, and reversing at intersections is banned. So you reach a missed exit by going round the roundabout once more.

questions.q: A temporary sign on a yellow background allows only a right turn, and a traffic controller signals you to go straight ahead. What should you do?
options: Turn right: the temporary sign is more important
Go straight ahead on the traffic controller’s signal
Stop and wait until the sign is removed
Choose either of the two directions
questions.explain: The signals and instructions of a traffic controller must be obeyed even if they contradict traffic lights, road signs (including temporary ones) or road markings.

questions.q: You have a red light and a green left arrow in a filter arrow section. Before the intersection there is a sign, as in the diagram. Which path may you take?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: A green left arrow normally allows a U-turn too, but only if it is not banned by a sign. Sign 3.19 bans U-turns, so you may only turn left (A), giving way to traffic from other directions.

questions.q: Under sign 5.15 “Parking place” there is plate 7.7. May you leave your car at this parking place with the engine running to keep the air conditioning on?
options: Yes, if you stay in the car
Yes, if the engine is diesel
No: only with the engine switched off
Yes, if it is hotter than 30°C outside
questions.explain: Plate 7.7 means that at a parking place marked by sign 5.15, parking is allowed only for vehicles with the engine not running.

questions.q: Under sign 5.15 there is plate 7.9 saying “2 h”. You left your car for 3 hours. Did you break the rules?
options: No: the plate is only a recommendation
Yes: parking here is limited to 2 hours
No, if you pay for the extra hour
No: the limit applies only to trucks
questions.explain: Plate 7.9 shows the maximum duration of parking at a place with sign 5.15. Here it is 2 hours, and you may not park for longer.

questions.q: Under sign 3.28 “No parking” there is plate 7.11 saying “7 t”. May you park here a van with a maximum authorised mass of 3.5 t?
options: Yes: the ban is for vehicles over 7 t only
No: the sign bans parking for everyone
No: the plate makes the ban stricter for vans
Yes, but for no longer than 7 minutes
questions.explain: Plate 7.11 means that the sign applies only to vehicles whose maximum authorised mass is greater than the one shown on the plate. A 3.5 t van is lighter than 7 t, so the parking ban does not apply to it.

questions.q: Under sign 3.28 “No parking” there is a plate “Except type of vehicle” showing a passenger car. Who is banned from parking?
options: Only passenger cars
Everyone except passenger cars
Nobody: the plate cancels the sign
Everyone, including passenger cars
questions.explain: Plates 7.4.9-7.4.14 show the type of vehicle to which the sign does not apply. Passenger cars may park here, and all others are banned.

questions.q: Under sign 5.15 “Parking place” there is plate 7.22 showing an electric car. May you park an ordinary petrol car here?
options: Yes, if all places for electric cars are free
Yes, if you park for no longer than an hour
No: this place is for electric cars
Yes, but only at night
questions.explain: Plate 7.22 limits the sign to electric cars and hybrid cars that are charged from an external source. So this parking place is intended only for them.
